questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said, 'I am happy.'

options.option_text: She said that she is happy.
She said that she was happy.
She said that I am happy.
She told she was happy.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Past reporting verb ('said') → tense shifts: 'am' → 'was'; pronoun 'I' → 'she'. 'Tell' requires an object, so 'told she' is wrong.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'I will go tomorrow.'

options.option_text: He said that he would go the next day.
He said that he will go tomorrow.
He said he went the next day.
He told that he would go the next day.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Tense shifts: 'will' → 'would'; 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'. 'Tell' requires an object; 'told that' is incorrect without an object before 'that'.

questions.stem: Change to direct speech: She said that she was tired.

options.option_text: She said, 'I am tired.'
She said, 'I was tired.'
She said, 'She is tired.'
She told, 'I am tired.'

questions.explanation: A is correct. Reverse the shift: 'was' → 'am'; 'she' → 'I'. Option D uses 'told' without an object, which is incorrect.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, 'Be quiet.'

options.option_text: The teacher told the students to be quiet.
The teacher said the students to be quiet.
The teacher asked the students that they be quiet.
The teacher told the students that be quiet.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Imperatives in indirect speech use 'told/asked/ordered + object + to + infinitive'.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said, 'Did you finish the work?'

options.option_text: He asked if I had finished the work.
He asked whether you finished the work.
He asked that if I had finished the work.
He said had I finished the work.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Yes/no questions → 'asked + if/whether + subject + verb'. Tense shifts: 'did finish' → 'had finished'. 'That + if' together is wrong.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said, 'How beautiful the sunset is!'

options.option_text: She exclaimed that the sunset was very beautiful.
She said that the sunset is beautiful.
She exclaimed how beautiful the sunset was.
She told the sunset was beautiful.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Exclamatory sentences → 'exclaimed that + assertive sentence (with appropriate tense shift and an adverb like very/quite)'. Option C lacks the declarative restructuring required.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: He said to me, 'Please help me.'

options.option_text: He requested me to help him.
He said to me to help him.
He told me that please help him.
He asked me please to help him.

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Please' in direct speech signals a polite request → 'requested + object + to + infinitive'.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said, 'I have been working since morning.'

options.option_text: She said that she had been working since morning.
She said she has been working since morning.
She said she was working since morning.
She told she had been working from morning.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous: 'had been working'. 'Since morning' stays as 'since morning' (it marks a point, not a duration). 'From morning' is incorrect for this context.

questions.stem: Change to direct speech: He asked whether she had come alone.

options.option_text: He said, 'Had she come alone?'
He said, 'Did she come alone?'
He asked, 'Did she come alone?'
He asked, 'Has she come alone?'

questions.explanation: C is correct. Reverse tense shift: 'had come' → 'Did...come' (past simple question). The reporting verb 'asked' signals a question; 'asked,' with quotation marks is correct.

questions.stem: Change to indirect speech (optative): Mother said, 'May God bless you, my child!'

options.option_text: Mother wished that God might bless her child.
Mother said God should bless her child.
Mother prayed that God might bless her child.
Mother exclaimed that God bless her child.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Sentences with 'May' expressing a blessing/prayer → indirect speech uses 'prayed that...might'. 'Wished' is used for personal desires, not divine blessings.
